record.paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
record.original_question: Let z(N0) be a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal, and let L^{APP}_z be the corresponding operator ideal of Banach-space operators. For inessential operators, the paper defines a trace to be spectral when its value is determined by the eigenvalue sequence of the operator. Show that every trace on L^{APP}_z is spectral whenever z(N0) is quasi-Banach.

evidence.quote:
Problem 8. Show that all traces on LAPP
z are spectral whenever z(N0) is
quasi-Banach.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $c_{00}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ denote sequences of complex numbers indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0 = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$ that are eventually zero. A sequence ideal $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0) \subseteq c_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a linear subspace closed under the pointwise action of $\ell_\infty$. It is called shift-monotone if it is invariant under the right shift $S_r(\xi_0,\xi_1,\dots) = (0,\xi_0,\xi_1,\dots)$ and the left shift $S_l(\xi_0,\xi_1,\dots) = (\xi_1,\xi_2,\dots)$. A quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal is such an ideal endowed with a complete quasi-norm $\|\cdot\|_{\mathfrak z}$ for which the shifts are bounded.

To such an ideal $\mathfrak z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ associate the operator ideal $\mathfrak L^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak z}$ consisting of all operators $T: X \to Y$ between Banach spaces whose approximation-number sequence $(a_n(T))_{n\ge 0}$ belongs to $\mathfrak z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, where $a_n(T) = \inf\{\|T - F\| : \operatorname{rank} F < n\}$ (with the convention $a_0(T)=\|T\|$).

A trace on $\mathfrak L^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak z}$ is a linear functional $\tau$ defined on the components $\mathfrak L^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak z}(X,X)$ for all Banach spaces $X$ such that $\tau(BA) = \tau(AB)$ whenever the composition makes sense and the trace property is well-defined within the ideal.

An operator $T \in \mathfrak L^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak z}(X,X)$ is inessential and its eigenvalue sequence $(\lambda_n(T))_{n\ge 0}$ is the sequence of nonzero eigenvalues counted with algebraic multiplicity, arranged in order of nonincreasing modulus, completed by zeros. A trace $\tau$ on $\mathfrak L^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak z}$ is called spectral if $\tau(T)$ depends only on $(\lambda_n(T))_{n\ge 0}$ for every $T$ in the ideal.

Problem. Prove that whenever $\mathfrak z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal, every trace on the operator ideal $\mathfrak L^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak z}$ is spectral.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of spectrality of all traces on $\mathfrak L^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak z}$ for quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals $\mathfrak z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is posed as an open problem in Pietsch's program on traces on Banach-space operator ideals. Web search did not surface any subsequent paper resolving it; related work (e.g. constructions of quasi-Banach operator ideals with strange/non-spectral traces) suggests subtleties remain. Status appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey collecting open problems including spectrality of traces on L^APP_z for quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed among the open problems.

status_evidence.title: Quasi-Banach operator ideals with a very strange trace
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of quasi-Banach operator ideals admitting nonzero continuous traces that vanish on finite-rank operators (related to spectrality issues).
status_evidence.claim: Subtleties of trace spectrality in the quasi-Banach setting are documented.
